title: MySQL: Improve Query Attribute decoding
description:
MySQL Query Attributes are key/value pairs that are send along with COM_QUERY and COM_STMT_EXECUTE. They are very similar to the bind parameters for prepared queries, but they are named.

This improves the Query Attribute decoding by making it more similar to prepared statement parameters

Resources:
- https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/query-attributes.html
- https://archive.fosdem.org/2021/schedule/event/mysql_protocl/
- https://dev.mysql.com/doc/dev/mysql-server/latest/page_protocol_com_stmt_prepare.html
- https://dev.mysql.com/doc/dev/mysql-server/latest/page_protocol_com_query.html

Capture:

One solution would be to have it look like this:
```
Attribute Definition (0)
    Type: FIELD_TYPE_STRING (254)
    Attribute Flags: 0x00
    Attribute Name: foo
Attribute Definition (1)
    Type: FIELD_TYPE_TIME (11)
    Attribute Flags: 0x00
    Attribute Name: bar
Attribute Value (0)
    Value (String): test test
Attribute Value (1)
    Length: 12
    Flags: Positive (0)
    Days: 0
    Hour: 8
    Minute: 23
    Second: 24
    Billionth of a second: 987654
```

This numbers and groups the definitions and the values.

I think this would be best, but more difficult to do:
```
Query Attribute
    Query Attribute Definition
        Type: FIELD_TYPE_STRING (254)
        Attribute Flags: 0x00
        Attribute Name: foo
    Query Attribute Value
        Value (String): test test
Query Attribute 
    Query Attribute Definition
        Type: FIELD_TYPE_TIME (11)
        Attribute Flags: 0x00
        Attribute Name: bar
    Query Attribute Value
        Length: 12
        Flags: Positive (0)
        Days: 0
        Hour: 8
        Minute: 23
        Second: 24
        Billionth of a second: 987654
```

This would group the values together with the definition.
I haven't yet tested this with prepared statements
move to draft status ?

Now tested with prepared statement parameters and Query Attributes with the following code:

```python
#!/bin/python3
import mysql.connector

con = mysql.connector.connect(host='127.0.0.1',user='root',database='test',ssl_disabled=True)

cur = con.cursor(prepared=True)
cur.execute('drop table if exists t1')
cur.execute('create table t1 (id bigint unsigned primary key, i bigint unsigned not null)')

cur.add_attribute('test', 'first')
cur.execute('insert into t1 (id, i) values (%s, %s)', (1, 123))

cur.clear_attributes()
cur.add_attribute('test', 'second')
cur.execute('insert into t1 (id, i) values (%s, %s)', (2, 456))
cur.close()
con.close()
```

i think it will be better to group (you can look packet-gquic.c if remember, there is already the same case)

May be you can also append the top item ? for don't need to all expend 

`Query Attribute : bar(type_time): 0 Days, 8 hour, 23 minutes... `
